matches.quote: a single Ti substituent already lowers the local symmetry from C6 to C2... through both its scattering potential and its strain field.
Unless the Ti data reach the standard of the Sn data... noting that the observables differ (½Q QPI for Sn, Bragg modulation for Ti).
state explicitly what distinguishes "domains of electronic nematicity" from "local C2 perturbations of individual dopants or dopant clusters".
For x ≈ 0.1 in particular, the text reports only stripe correlations and no ½Q_Bragg features... so it is unclear what evidence for nematic domains exists there
the Sn-sample evidence is unidirectional modulation at finite q ≈ ½Q_Bragg, which describes a local unidirectional density wave (smectic-like)
Short-range, disorder-pinned 2×2 CDW correlations are not excluded, so the claim that the anisotropy is "unrelated to the 2 × 2 charge density wave" is not established
Random Ti placement would therefore produce patches of twofold Bragg-amplitude anisotropy in three orientations, with boundaries between them, without any electronic nematic order
the statement that pristine-compound phenomena "may arise from the electronic nematic state imaged here" (p. 7) is not supported by the paper's own data.
